title: "Class notebooks"

## Instructor: live Titanic exploration

Open **`notebooks/titanic_live_scaffold.ipynb`** in Positron. Setup is complete, while the analysis cells contain prompts to fill in live. Open **`titanic_complete.ipynb`** in a second tab for reference or recovery.

The two versions have matching sections:

1. Understand the passenger records and missing information.
2. Optionally revisit the opening fare histogram.
3. Count survivors by passenger class.
4. Compare survival proportions using all passengers in each class.
5. Add recorded sex through color and interpret the comparison.

| Version | Notebook download | Browser preview |
|---|---|---|
| Live scaffold | [titanic_live_scaffold.ipynb](notebooks/titanic_live_scaffold.ipynb) | [Read online](notebooks/titanic_live_scaffold.html) |
| Completed | [titanic_complete.ipynb](notebooks/titanic_complete.ipynb) | [Read online](notebooks/titanic_complete.html) |

## Students: tornado starter

Open **`notebooks/tornadoes_starter.ipynb`**. The first cells load the bundled CSV, preview a few records, show column types, and check missing information. The data guide explains units and interpretation. The final cells are open for your question and visualizations.

[Download the tornado starter](notebooks/tornadoes_starter.ipynb) · [Read the starter online](notebooks/tornadoes_starter.html)

## Optional plotting reference

Examples use Titanic rather than prescribing a tornado investigation. Use the histogram, grouped comparison, scatterplot, or count/proportion example that helps with your own question.

[Download the plotting reference](notebooks/plotting_reference.ipynb) · [Read online](notebooks/plotting_reference.html)

## Local setup

Open the whole project folder in Positron, then run:

```bash
uv sync
```

Select the interpreter in `.venv` as the notebook kernel. Run the setup cell before class. Dependencies install once, and the data then load locally.

Restart the kernel and clear outputs in the live scaffold whenever you want a fresh teaching copy. Edit a copy if you want to keep the supplied scaffold unchanged.
